what_it_does: CXL (Compute Express Link) is a high-speed connector standard that lets a computer expand its working memory or storage by attaching extra modules over a cable, similar to plugging in a fast external drive but at far higher speeds and tighter integration. The promise is that servers can add cheap memory on demand, but in practice the CXL-attached memory or storage slows down when it has to share the same physical links with the computer's regular memory and storage — a problem called interference. This paper is the first systematic study of that interference on real CXL hardware, using built-in performance counters and tracing tools to reverse-engineer exactly what causes the slowdowns. It also proposes and tests fixes to reduce the interference.
